title: Task model routing and direct ZAI Flash audit

exclusions: No production deployment or broad task-quality benchmark is claimed.

findings.text: Bounded tasks shared a full GLM 5.3 default; explicitly modelled candidates ignore a changed provider default_model.
Both direct ZAI models returned semantically correct JSON on all three paired synthetic tasks. Flash mean latency was 5.281s versus 4.824s for full GLM at low effort.
Direct Flash can reduce Coding Plan use for bounded roles; the documented multipliers applied to observed tokens imply about 58% fewer points in this sample.
Validate large-context assessment quality and task success after independent publication and deployment.

checks.name: Paired synthetic task correctness
checks.reason: Task IDs, action, lane, IDE and install=false checked for three examples per model.

checks.name: Production quality and deployed candidate
checks.reason: No production replay or candidate deployment; source change is owned by ticket-177.

limitations: Three tiny canaries cannot establish production quality or latency percentiles.
The larger Supervisor context has not been replayed.
Provider success does not establish task success; historical attempts used different contexts.
